In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $(2x+1)(y+1),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit. 

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $y+1,$ and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $2x+1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x}{2x+1}-\frac{2y}{y+1} & = \\ \frac{y+1}{y+1}\cdot \frac{4x}{2x+1}-\frac{2x+1}{2x+1}\cdot \frac{2y}{y+1} & = \\ \frac{4x(y+1)}{(2x+1)(y+1)}-\frac{(2x+1)2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & = \\ \frac{4x(y+1)-(2x+1)2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & = \\ \frac{4xy+4x-4xy-2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & = \\ \frac{4x-2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & \end{aligned}
$$
